The fixed-size array changes from 24 to 16 characters; this is a real wire-layout change. The consumer read is a nested Gid.data access, not merely a matching symbol name. A substantive layout difference does not by itself refute the resolved label: the specification describes consumer-side rejection/hardening rather than layout convergence: snapshot:specs/C3-099.json:120
"    "summary": "Consumer-side hardening, not removal of the mismatch: the generated CDR deserializers check a sequence length read from the wire against the remaining buffer before resizing and fail the sample instead (rosidl_typesupport_fastrtps templates, rolling 7283329f7c3cb654e7b843ab127ab2eda680662a, humble backport f7e1095e7fd5f9d69c127e7c179c680d5ca70612 released in 2.2.3, which requires rebuilding rmw_dds_common's humble typesupport); counterpart for rmw_fastrtps_dynamic_cpp in rmw_fastrtps (rolling 09e5a5f1b9504431bbc8970bb098438041041dbe, humble 197c1852f1c780728b3add675bf30b316e02458d). The humble consumer still receives jazzy/rolling ParticipantEntitiesInfo samples with the 16-byte Gid layout and now discards them with a printed error. Maintainers also proposed (not implemented in the sources) refusing peers with/without type hashes, and suggested ROS_DOMAIN_ID separation or ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST as workarounds.","
